3. The present bail application under Section 439 of Cr.P.C. has been filed by the Petitioner for regular bail in connection with C.T. Case No.703 of 2023, arising out of 1.C.C. No.22 of 2023, corresponding to Brajrajnagar P.S. Case No.199 of 2023, pending in the Court of learned J.M.F.C.-1 (Cog. Taking), Jharsuguda, for alleged commission of offence punishable under Sections 419 / 420 / 467 / 468 / 471 / 409 / 406 / 34 of I.P.C.

He further contended that investigation has progressed substantially in the meantime and the charge sheet is likely to be filed very soon.

Further referring to the allegation made in the F.I.R., learned counsel for the Petitioner submitted that out of alleged amount of Rs.30,00,000/-, a sum of Rs.6,00,000/- has been transferred to the account of the present Petitioner.
He further contended that the Petitioner does not have any criminal antecedent.
He also contended that the Petitioner belongs to the locality, therefore, there is no chance of absconding.

Learned counsel for the Petitioner further drawing attention to the order dated 10.04.2024 passed by this Court in ABLAPL No.9658 of 2023, submitted that a co-accused, namely, Pinku Mandal has already been released on bail vide order passed by a coordinate Bench of this Court in ABLAPL No.9658 of 2023 subject to the condition that he shall deposit a sum of Rs.1,50,000/-.

He further contended that the Petitioner is ready and willing to return the money which was transferred from the account of the Informant to the account of the Petitioner, i.e. a sum of Rs.6,00,000/-.

In view of the aforesaid development, learned counsel for the Petitioner submitted that the Petitioner be released on bail on any terms and conditions that would be imposed by this Court and that the Petitioner shall abide by such terms and conditions and shall cooperate with the investigation as well as early conclusion of the trial.
5. Learned counsel for the Informant submitted that the allegations made in the F.I.R. are very serious in nature.
He further contended that the Petitioner has cheated the Informant and had taken away a sum of Rs.30,00,000/- and jewellery belonging to the Informant.
He further contended that taking advantage of the innocence of the Informant, the Petitioner and other co-accused persons had taken away the money from the Informant.
It was also contended that the investigation is still on, therefore, the release of the Petitioner would cause serious prejudice in concluding the investigation.
On such ground, learned counsel for the Informant submitted that the Petitioner should not be enlarged on bail at this stage.

6. Learned counsel for the State while supporting the stand of the learned counsel for the Informant,
submitted that considering the gravity and seriousness of the allegation made in the F.I.R., the Petitioner should not be released on bail.

He further submitted that in the event the Petitioner is released on bail, there is every likelihood the Petitioner might abscond from justice which would eventually cause delay in concluding the investigation and also early conclusion of the trial.

7. Having heard the learned counsels appearing for the respective parties and on careful examination of the materials on record as well as upon conspectus of the surrounding facts and circumstances of the present case and further taking into consideration the period of custodial detention and the fact that one of the co-accused has already been released on bail by a coordinate Bench of this Court, this Court is inclined to release the Petitioner on bail.

8. Hence, it is directed that the Petitioner be released on bail in the aforesaid case on furnishing bail bond of Rs.50,000/-(Rupees fifty thousand) with two local solvent sureties each for the like amount to the satisfaction of the Court in seisin over the matter.
The release of the Petitioner shall also be subject to the condition that he shall refund the amount of Rs.6,00,000/- (Rupees six lakhs) to the Informant at the time of his release on bail.
In addition to the above, the Petitioner shall also furnish property security to the tune of Rs.5,00,000/- (Rupees five lakhs).
